ai.literal: his heart to him becoming even having seen why O heart you to me not becoming
ai.translation: O my heart! Even after seeing that his heart belongs to him, why do you not belong to me?
ai.modern: நெஞ்சே! அவருடைய நெஞ்சம் அவருக்கே துணையாக இருப்பதைப் பார்த்த பின்பும், நீ எனக்குத் துணையாக இல்லாமல் அவரிடம் செல்வது ஏன்?
ai.explanation: The heroine addresses her own heart in a moment of romantic conflict. She observes that her lover's heart remains steadfastly loyal to him, not yielding to her desires. Seeing this, she questions why her own heart does not show the same loyalty to her, but instead abandons her to side with him. The contrast between his heart becoming his and her heart not becoming hers highlights her helplessness in love.

ai.literal: Him who does not love seen even at the time, him 'he will not be angry' saying you go, my heart.
ai.translation: O my heart! Even when you see that he does not love us, you go to him thinking, 'He will not be angry.'
ai.modern: என் நெஞ்சே! நம்மிடம் அன்பு இல்லாதவரைக் கண்டபோதும், அவர் நம்மை வெறுக்க மாட்டார் என்று நினைத்து அவரிடமே நீ செல்கிறாய்.
ai.explanation: The speaker chides her own heart for its weakness in love. Even when she clearly sees that her lover is not attached to her (உறாஅதவர்), her heart still rushes to him. It justifies this surrender by naively thinking that he will at least not be angry or reject her (செறாஅர்). The couplet captures the helplessness of a heart that refuses to hold a grudge.

ai.literal: To the ruined, friends are not, is that the saying, O heart, you, as desired, his behind going?
ai.translation: O heart, is it because of the saying 'the ruined have no friends' that you abandon me to follow him as you please?
ai.modern: நெஞ்சே! கெட்டுப்போனவர்களுக்கு நண்பர்கள் இல்லை என்ற பழமொழியை நினைத்துத்தானோ, நீ உனக்கு விருப்பமானபடி அவர் பின்னால் செல்கிறாய்?
ai.explanation: The heroine addresses her own heart, which seems to have abandoned her to go after her lover. She wonders if her heart is acting on the old proverb that those who are ruined have no friends. Since she is ruined by lovesickness, her heart has deserted her to follow its own desire, leaving her completely alone. The word 'பெட்டாங்கு' means acting exactly as one desires, highlighting the heart's betrayal.

ai.literal: Hereafter such things with you will consult who, O heart! Sulk having made, you do not enjoy, see, further.
ai.translation: O heart, who will ever consult you about such things hereafter? You initiate a sulk, but then you fail to see it through and enjoy it!
ai.modern: நெஞ்சே! நீ ஊடல் கொள்கிறாய், ஆனால் அதை இறுதிவரை அனுபவிக்காமல் விட்டுவிடுகிறாய். இனிமேல் இப்படிப்பட்ட காரியங்களை உன்னோடு யார் ஆலோசிப்பார்கள்?
ai.explanation: The speaker addresses her own heart, frustrated by its inconsistency in matters of love. The heart eagerly initiates a sulk (feigned anger) with the lover, but quickly gives it up without fully experiencing or sustaining it. Because the heart abandons its resolve so easily, the speaker declares she will no longer consult it on such matters. The word 'துவ்வாய்' (from the root 'துவ்வு', to enjoy or experience) highlights the heart's failure to actually sustain the resentment it started.

ai.literal: Non-obtaining it fears; if obtained, separation it fears; unceasing sorrow-having [is] my heart.
ai.translation: My heart fears when it cannot attain him, and fears separation when it does. Thus, it is afflicted with unceasing sorrow.
ai.modern: அவரைப் பெற முடியாதபோது என் நெஞ்சம் அஞ்சுகிறது; அவரைப் பெற்றாலோ மீண்டும் பிரிந்துவிடுவோமோ என்று அஞ்சுகிறது. அதனால் என் நெஞ்சம் நீங்காத துன்பத்தை உடையதாக இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker addresses the constant state of anxiety in her heart regarding her lover. When he is away, the heart fears that it might not attain him again. When he is present, it immediately fears the inevitable future separation. Because it is caught between these two fears, the heart is burdened with endless, unceasing sorrow. The poetic lengthening of vowels (alapeṭai) in words like 'பெறாஅமை' (non-obtaining) and 'அறாஅ' (unceasing) emphasizes the prolonged and continuous nature of her suffering.

ai.literal: Alone having been when thought me to eat it was my heart.
ai.translation: When I sit alone and think of him, my heart is ready to consume me.
ai.modern: நான் தனியாக இருந்து அவரைப் பற்றி நினைத்தால், என் நெஞ்சம் என்னைத் தின்பது போலத் துன்புறுத்துகிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker describes the intense pain of separation. When she sits alone and reflects on her lover, her own heart turns against her. Instead of comforting her, it torments her so deeply that it feels as though it is eating her alive. The word 'தினிய' vividly captures this consuming agony.

ai.literal: Even modesty I forgot, him unable to forget my lacking dignity foolish heart-in having been caught.
ai.translation: Caught in my undignified, foolish heart that cannot forget him, I have forgotten even my modesty.
ai.modern: அவரை மறக்க முடியாத என்னுடைய மாண்பில்லாத முட்டாள் நெஞ்சத்திடம் அகப்பட்டு, நான் என் நாணத்தையும் மறந்துவிட்டேன்.
ai.explanation: The speaker chides her own heart for its weakness. She says her heart is foolish and lacks dignity because it refuses to forget the lover who has left her. By being caught in the sway of such a heart, she finds herself longing for him openly, thus forgetting even her natural modesty.

ai.literal: If despised, it will be a disgrace saying, having considered, his virtues thinks of, the life-loving heart.
ai.translation: Thinking, It would be a disgrace to despise him, my heart, whose love is as dear as life, dwells only on his virtues.
ai.modern: அவரை இகழ்ந்து ஊடினால் அது நமக்குச் சிறுமையாகும் என்று கருதி, என் உயிரைப் போன்ற அன்புடைய நெஞ்சம் அவருடைய நல்ல குணங்களையே நினைக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker is frustrated with her own heart because it refuses to be angry with her lover. Her heart reasons that sulking or despising him would only bring disgrace to their deep bond. Because its love for him is as precious as life itself, the heart chooses to remember only his good qualities instead of his faults.

ai.literal: To sorrow who indeed companion will become, oneself possessing heart companion not when?
ai.translation: When one's own heart is not a supportive companion, who indeed will be a companion in sorrow?
ai.modern: தம்முடைய நெஞ்சமே தமக்குத் துணையாகாத போது, வரும் துன்பத்திற்கு வேறு யார் துணையாவார்?
ai.explanation: The speaker is suffering from love-sickness and feels betrayed by their own heart, which yields to the lover instead of staying firm. When one's very own heart refuses to be a supportive companion, there is no one else who can help bear the sorrow. The word 'வழி' here means 'the time when' or 'the state in which'.

ai.literal: Natural one's-own-people they-are-not strangers, oneself possessing heart one's-own-people not when.
ai.translation: When one's own heart does not act as an ally, it is only natural that strangers do not act as friends.
ai.modern: தம்முடைய நெஞ்சமே தமக்கு உறவாக இல்லாத போது, அயலார் உறவாக இல்லாதிருப்பது இயற்கையானதே.
ai.explanation: The speaker is frustrated with her own heart for betraying her resolve and yielding to her lover. She reflects that if her very own heart does not act as her ally, she cannot expect strangers to be supportive. The word 'tañcam' here takes the classical meaning of 'easy' or 'natural consequence', emphasizing that the lack of support from others is entirely expected when one is betrayed by one's own mind.
